'''Alexander Steinkasserer''' (born 1958 in [[Bruneck]], [[Italy]]), is a German-Italian [[immunologist]] and professor. He is the Head of the Department of Immune Modulation at the [[University Hospital Erlangen]] of the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg]] (FAU). His research focuses on the biology of [[dendritic cell]]s, specifically the immunomodulatory properties of the [[CD83]] molecule. He is also a member of the University Council of the [[Free University of Bozen-Bolzano]].

== Education and early career ==
Steinkasserer studied biology at the [[University of Innsbruck]], where he received his PhD in 1984. From 1986 to 1989, he worked as a postdoctoral researcher at [[LMU Munich]]. He then moved to the [[University of Oxford]], where he was a research fellow at the Department of Biochemistry and the MRC Immunochemistry Unit under Robert B. Sim from 1989 to 1993.<ref name="FAU_CV">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. rer. nat. Alexander Steinkasserer: CV |url=https://www.sfb1607.de/en/team-member/prof-dr-rer-nat-alexander-steinkasserer-dept/ |publisher=Collaborative Research Centre 1607 |access-date=2026-02-14}}</ref>

Between 1993 and 1996, Steinkasserer served as a Laboratory Head at the [[Novartis]] Research Institute in Vienna, followed by a position as Division Head at [[Baxter International|Baxter]] (Vienna) from 1996 to 1998.<ref name="FAU_CV"/> In 1996, he completed his [[Habilitation]] in Molecular Biology at the [[University of Vienna]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Curriculum vitae Prof. Dr. Alexander Steinkasserer |url=https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/University/University-Council/2023-12-18-steinkasserer-CV-en.pdf |page=1 |access-date=2026-02-14}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
In 1998, Steinkasserer was appointed Professor and Head of the Department of Immune Modulation at the University Hospital Erlangen (FAU Erlangen–Nuremberg).<ref name="FAU_CV"/>

His scientific work centers on the immune system's regulation, particularly the role of dendritic cells and the surface molecule [[CD83]]. His group was among the first to describe the soluble form of CD83 (sCD83) and its therapeutic potential in autoimmune diseases and transplantation.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zinser |first1=Elisabeth |last2=Lechmann |first2=Matthias |last3=Golka |first3=Antje |last4=Lutz |first4=Manfred B. |last5=Steinkasserer |first5=Alexander |title=Prevention and treatment of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis by soluble CD83 |journal=The Journal of Experimental Medicine |date=2004-08-02 |volume=200 |issue=3 |pages=345–351 |doi=10.1084/jem.20030973 |pmid=15289503 |pmc=2211980}}</ref> He has published over 200 peer-reviewed articles and has an [[h-index]] of 60.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alexander Steinkasserer |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=GW59LPIAAAAJ&hl=en |publisher=Google Scholar |access-date=2026-02-14}}</ref>

Steinkasserer is also involved in translational research. He is a co-founder of Mallia Innovations (formerly Mallia Therapeutics), a spin-off established to translate CD83 research into therapeutic applications. The project was awarded the m4 Award by the Bavarian Ministry of Economic Affairs in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=m4 Award Winners |url=https://www.m4-award.org/en/winners.html |publisher=BioM Biotech Cluster Development GmbH |access-date=2026-02-14}}</ref>

In addition to his role in Erlangen, Steinkasserer serves on the University Council of the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano in Italy.<ref>{{cite web |title=University Council |url=https://www.unibz.it/en/home/organisation/university-council/ |publisher=Free University of Bozen-Bolzano |access-date=2026-02-14}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* 1991: Futura Award for South Tyroleans abroad<ref name="FAU_CV"/>
* 2003: Research Prize of the Berlin Foundation for Dermatology<ref>{{cite web |title=Preisträger der Stiftung und Förderungen |url=http://stiftung-dermatologie.de/preistraeger-der-stiftung-und-foerderungen/ |publisher=Berliner Stiftung für Dermatologie |language=de |access-date=2026-02-14}}</ref>
* 2006: Paul Langerhans Award of the Arbeitsgemeinschaft Dermatologische Forschung (ADF)<ref>{{cite web |title=Paul Langerhans Award of the ADF |url=https://adf-online.de/preise/paul-langerhans-award-of-the-adf/ |publisher=Arbeitsgemeinschaft Dermatologische Forschung |language=en |access-date=2026-02-14}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
* Leachman, M., et al. (2001). "Dendritic cells generated from blood monocytes of HIV-1 patients are not infected and can be used for vaccinations." ''[[Journal of Immunology]]''.
* Zinser, E., et al. (2004). "Prevention and treatment of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis by soluble CD83." ''[[Journal of Experimental Medicine]]''.
* Prechtel, A.T., & Steinkasserer, A. (2007). "CD83: an update on functions and prospects of the maturational marker of dendritic cells." ''[[Immunology]]''.
